messages.author: 4dd9d775fef6ed8d
messages.subject: Simple AJAX jQuery rApache Example
parts:
I'm trying to post data from a form to an R script via JSON, execute the R script, return the results as a JSON array, and place certain elements of array in a div in the HTML doc. 
I'm using jQuery for the ajax post, code is below. The data makes a round trip, but the R script does not execute. How do I fix it? Also how do I get the response as JSON instead of text?

Here is "ex1.html":

<!doctype html>
<head> <meta charset="utf-8">
<title>Rapache Ajax JQuery R Example</title>
<script src="http://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jquery/1.8.1/jquery.min.js"></script>
<script>
 $(document).ready(function(){
    $("#b1").click(function(){
      formdata = $("form").serializeArray();
      console.log("this is the form data: ",  formdata);
      $.post("/cindy_Rscripts/test.R" , formdata, function(){
         console.log("this is the returned data: ", responseText);
         $("#result").html(responseText);
      });    });   });
</script>
</head>
<body>
<form>
  <p>word:             <input name="word1" type="text"></p>
  <p>another word: <input name="word2" type="text"></p>
  <input id="b1" value="Go" type="button">
  <div id="result"></div>
  <div id="mydiv">This is my div!</div>
</form></body></html>

Here is "test.R" (I've tested it in the console and it works):

## get the RJSONIO library to manipulate JSON arrays from the POST
require(RJSONIO, lib.loc="/usr/lib/R/lib")

## check to see if POST data is valid JSON
if(isValidJSON(POST,TRUE)) { print("Good -- it's valid JSON")}

## create a dataframe from the POST
df <-data.frame(fromJSON(POST, simplifyWithNames=FALSE))

## print this out to see if it works and where it goes
nms <- names(df)
print(paste("the names in the array are: ", nms))
print(paste("word1 = ", df$word1))
print(paste("word2 = ", df$word2))
print(paste("the structure of the dataframe is : ", str(df)))

Here is a snippet from bottom of  "apache2.conf":

LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
# this works
<Location /RApacheInfo>
SetHandler r-info
</Location>
# this works from the rApache Cookbook on www.rapache.net/manual
<Location /rapachetest>
SetHandler r-handler
RFileHandler /var/www/R/test2.R
</Location>
# I added this and it seems to work but not sure if it's correct for my situation
<FilesMatch "/var/www/cindy_Rscripts/test.R">
SetHandler r-script
RHandler base::sys.source
</FilesMatch>

Thanks in advance for any comments.
CB

messages.author: 42eed4e1caba0ad0
messages.subject: Re: Simple AJAX jQuery rApache Example
parts:
Are you sure that the script isn't executing? It should work, but you shouldn't get valid JSON output that jQuery can parse. Don't use print() but cat(). And before you cat() out the repsonse, put relevant parts to list in format like:

list(success = TRUE, output = <something>)

so that it can be serialised properly. The way you're doing it is not returning JSON, but bunch of text. And you may defer loading of text data to JS instead of R (the paste()/print() stuff can and should be handled with JS). Speaking of JS, I'd recommend slightly more hackish .ajax() function, but .post() should work just fine, just skim down the documentation for more options (.post() options are practically the same as in .ajax()). You may want to set dataType: "json" and return JSON from your R script. Right now you aren't generating any JSON (see documentation for toJSON()).

I have pretty outdated webapp here, with some deprecated RApache directives, but if you read the source, you'll see how it's handled. I also strongly recommend Jeroen Ooms' video.

aL3xa

parts:
I finally got the simple example working by using  receiveBin()
Thanks to Jeff for it (and Alex for suggestions), and Jeroen's videos/slides, and hundreds of web pages.
It appends form data to other JSON data, posts to Rscript, runs it, returns modified JSON data to html doc.
I've spent hours studying and surfing to put all this stuff together -- not easy! 
You can watch the Net panel to see the post/response data.
Here it is -- I'd like to know if anyone finds it useful.

This is "ex1.html" , I've indicated which jQuery settings DON'T work when sending JSON to Rscripts

<!doctype html>
<head> <meta charset="utf-8">
<title>Rapache Ajax JQuery JSON R Example</title>

<script src="http://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jquery/1.8.1/jquery.min.js"></script>
<script>
 $(document).ready(function(){
    $("#b1").click(function(){

// Define the data packet that we are going to post to the
      // server. This will be "stringified" as a JSON value.
      var datatopost = {
        name: "Rocky",
        hair: "Brunette",
        favoriteMovies: ["Terminator 2", "The Notebook", "Teenwolf"] };

      formdata = JSON.stringify(datatopost);
      //THIS DOES NOT WORK!    formdata = JSON.stringify($("form").serializeArray() )
console.log("this is the form data: ",  formdata);

$.ajax({
         type: "POST",
         url: "/rscripts/test6.r",
         data: formdata,
        // THIS DOES NOT WORK!  processData: false,
        // THIS DOES NOT WORK!  dataType: "json",  
          contentType: "application/json" 
          });

      $("#result").ajaxSuccess(function(event, xhr, settings) {
           $(this).text('IT WORKS!!!       ' + xhr.responseText )
         });
      $("#result").ajaxError(function(event, xhr, settings) {
           $(this).text("Request failed");

});
  }); }); 
</script></head>

<body><form id="f1">
  <p>word: <input id="w1" name="word1" type="text"></p>
  <p>another word: <input id="w2" name="word2" type="text"></p>
<input id="b1" value="Go" type="button">

</form> <p><div id="result"></div></p>
<p><div id="mydiv">Oh MY!</div></p></p>
</form></body></html>

This is "/rscripts/test6.r" , receiveBin() makes it all possible! 
<!doctype html>
binpost  <- receiveBin()
postdata <- rawToChar(binpost)

 if (isValidJSON(postdata, TRUE)) {
    df <-data.frame(fromJSON(postdata, simplifyWithNames=FALSE))
    nms <- names(df)
    df$new1 <- c("toy")
    df$new2 <- c("boat")
    resdata <- toJSON(df)
    cat(resdata)
    }
  
Here's snippets from "/etc/apache2/apache2.conf" 
LoadModule R_module /usr/lib/apache2/modules/mod_R.so
# Load packages on startup

REvalOnStartup "require(RJSONIO, lib.loc='/usr/lib/R/lib')"

<Directory /var/www/rscripts>

SetHandler r-script
        RHandler base::sys.source

</Directory>

Your input/suggestions welcome!
Cindy
